title: Composition API Best Practices
description: Tips for organizing code and migrating from Options API.

slides.title: Organizing Your Code
Migration from Options API
slides.content:
# Gradual Adoption

- You can use Composition API alongside Options API in the same component.
- Migrate feature by feature: start with one computed property or watcher, move to `setup()`.
- Use `<script setup>` in Single‑File Components for a cleaner syntax.

**`<script setup>`** is a compile‑time syntactic sugar that makes Composition API more ergonomic. It reduces boilerplate and automatically exposes top‑level bindings to the template.

```vue
<script setup>
import { ref } from 'vue'
const count = ref(0)
</script>

<template>
  <button @click="count++">{{ count }}</button>
</template>
```

slides.title: TypeScript Integration
slides.content:
The Composition API is built with TypeScript in mind. When using `ref`, you can specify the type:

```typescript
const count = ref<number>(0)
const user = ref<User | null>(null)
```

`reactive` automatically infers types, but you can also annotate the returned object.

With `<script setup>`, the type system works seamlessly.

quizData.question: What is the recommended way to organize code inside `setup()`?

options.text: Group by logical feature or concern

quizData.explanation: Grouping code by logical feature improves readability and maintainability, as related code stays together.
